gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's SolarX 4K only accepts 150–500 V. With a BLUETTI SORA 500 panel at 49.1 V Voc, three panels in series give 147.3 V and fall short, so a single Apex 300 system needs at least four in series (196.4 V). BLUETTI's own 'Apex 300 + 2 × 500W' bundles cannot feed the SolarX 4K, and the SolarX comes as two $699 versions with different cables: P090D for one Apex 300, XT60 for parallel units.
standout_why: I compared against watthourlab.com/home-backup/transfer-switch-basics, a cited page I opened. It gives only wattage totals: 'Solar: 2600 W total' for the DELTA Pro 3 and '3,200 W (2 × 1600 W)' for the F3800 Plus. It gives no input voltage window, no panel models, no series count and no exclusions. Popular Mechanics, the other cited page, blocked fetching, so I could not check it, and that leaves some risk in this score. ChatGPT's own answer says nothing about voltage windows or cable versions. The finding decides the set: how many panels to buy, and which SolarX version.
kit_items: Battery/inverter: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh, 3,840 W, 120/240 V). It is on BLUETTI's US store, an approved program, and Dealectric already lists it. Anker's store returned HTTP 404 and the F3800 Plus kit page showed 'Sold Out', so Anker is out.
Expansion battery: BLUETTI B300K (adds 2,764.8 Wh for 5,529.6 Wh total). The SolarX 4K's compatibility list names it.

Home connection: BLUETTI Home Integration Kit, Single Apex 300 version. It contains a Reliance sub panel with a 50 A SS2-50 inlet box, a 50 A outlet box, a NEMA 14-50 to SS2-50R cable and a 50 A fast-charging cable 'for Apex 300 (Single Unit Use)'. The Parallel version costs $100 more and swaps in a parallel charging cable. Buy the version that matches how many Apex 300 units you have.
Solar controller: BLUETTI SolarX 4K with the Locking Terminal to P090D cable (for Single Use). Accepts 150–500 V and up to 4 kW. The XT60 version at the same price is for parallel Apex 300s.

Panels: 4 × BLUETTI SORA 500 (MC4) wired in series. Voc is 4 × 49.1 = 196.4 V, which clears the 150 V minimum, and Vmp is 4 × 40.92 = 163.7 V, inside Notebookcheck's listed 120–450 V MPPT range. That is 2,000 W of panels. Three panels give 147.3 V, below the minimum.

findings.label: Open-circuit voltage / Vmp / Isc
findings.value: Voc 49.1 V, Vmp 40.92 V, Isc 13.31 A
findings.source_title: The Bluetti Sora 500 Solar Panel Review – Impulse Gamer (Andrew Paul, 2026-08-02)
findings.note: Named reviewer. BLUETTI's US page has an empty Tech Specs section, and the EU page failed with a redirect loop. Arithmetic: 3S = 147.3 V Voc, below 150 V. 4S = 196.4 V Voc and 163.7 V Vmp, which fits. 10S = 491 V at STC, but cold weather raises Voc, so I would keep to about 9S. That margin is my own inference, not a BLUETTI figure.
